statements.label: supported
statements.text: A total of 555 candidate de novo genes were found in D. melanogaster, all of them having arisen within the Drosophilinae lineage.
statements.evidence: We identify 555 de novo gene candidates in D. melanogaster that originated within the Drosophilinae lineage.
statements.note: The abstract reports 555 de novo gene candidates in D. melanogaster that originated within the Drosophilinae lineage.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell RNA-seq of testis showed the majority of de novo gene candidates to be enriched in spermatocytes, while several young candidates leaned toward early spermatogenesis.
statements.evidence: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis in testis shows that although most de novo gene candidates are enriched in spermatocytes, several young candidates are biased towards the early spermatogenesis stage
statements.note: The testis single-cell RNA-seq analysis found most candidates enriched in spermatocytes and several young ones biased towards early spermatogenesis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: De novo gene candidates with well-folded protein structures are required for male fertility in D. melanogaster.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overall, the study detected only minor changes in protein structure among the de novo gene candidates from the Drosophilinae lineage.
statements.evidence: Surprisingly, we find little overall protein structural changes in candidates from the Drosophilinae lineage.
statements.note: The abstract states that, surprisingly, candidates from the Drosophilinae lineage showed little overall protein structural change.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.note: The abstract tests how splicing and U1 recognition affect nuclear export of this gene's RNA, but says nothing about where its protein localizes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking out ENSG00000205704 in human embryonic stem cells accelerated neuronal maturation in the cortical organoids derived from them.

statements.note: The abstract reports that knock-out of the gene accelerates, and over-expression delays, neuronal maturation of cortical organoids.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In 74 human- or hominoid-specific de novo genes, the study found characteristic U1 elements and splicing-related sequences responsible for exporting RNA from the nucleus.

statements.note: The abstract reports U1 elements and splice-related sequences accounting for RNA nuclear export in 74 human/hominoid-specific de novo genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ectopic expression of ENSG00000205704 in transgenic mice enlarged their brains and expanded the cortex.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Paddlefish and sturgeon lineages separated before rediploidization had progressed even halfway, which hides the fact that they share one genome duplication.
statements.evidence: We show that the sharing of this WGD is masked by the fact that paddlefish and sturgeon lineage divergence occurred before rediploidization had proceeded even half-way.
statements.note: The abstract explains that the shared WGD is masked because the two lineages diverged before rediploidization was even half complete.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Rediploidization proceeded faster in the sturgeon lineage than in the paddlefish lineage.
statements.evidence: This was followed by a prolonged process of reversion to stable diploid inheritance (rediploidization), that may have promoted survival during the Triassic-Jurassic mass extinction.
statements.note: The abstract describes rediploidization as prolonged and largely lineage-specific but never compares its pace between sturgeon and paddlefish.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The whole-genome duplication that paddlefish and sturgeon share is older than 200 million years.
statements.evidence: these derive from a shared genome duplication event occurring well over 200 million years ago, likely close to the Permian-Triassic mass extinction period
statements.note: The abstract dates the shared genome duplication to well over 200 million years ago.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For the majority of genes, the return to stable diploid inheritance happened separately in each of the two lineages.
statements.evidence: Thus, for most genes the resolution to diploidy was lineage-specific.
statements.note: The abstract states that for most genes the resolution to diploidy was lineage-specific.

statements.text: Beyond their promoter-proximal ACRs, C4 genes have on average two to three distal cell-type-specific ACRs, underlining how complex and divergent C4 evolution has been.
